scenario.description: A maintenance control officer must publish the next-workday priority order and work windows for three routine backup-power work orders, assigning the responsible section and recording the operational control for each job.

shared_context.S1: The next-workday maintenance board has open work orders for GEN-2, GEN-4, and UPS-1.
shared_context.S2: GEN-2 supports the facilities area, GEN-4 supports the clinic, and UPS-1 supports the communications shelter.
shared_context.S3: WO1 Grant signs the binding maintenance board, and the board must identify a priority order, work window, responsible section, and operational control for each work order.
shared_context.S4: Power Section, the Generator Team, and Signal Section can work separate assigned jobs during the day.
shared_context.S5: As part of the normal morning maintenance-board review, WO1 Grant checks each supported section for schedule restrictions before signing the board.

PF1.text: SFC Morales confirmed during the 0600 facilities inspection that GEN-2 has a coolant leak requiring lockout and repair in the exact 0800-1100 work window, with Power Section responsible; the inspection entry is still being entered into the maintenance system and is not on the draft board.

PF2.text: Capt. Shah confirmed that the clinic will run a vaccine-refrigerator validation from 0900 through 1300, so GEN-4 must remain online until 1300 and its maintenance window must be exactly 1300-1500. Generator Team is responsible for GEN-4, and the board must include a clinic-service deconfliction control; the clinic schedule was finalized after the draft board was circulated.

PF3.text: Lt. Okafor confirmed that UPS-1 battery replacement requires an uninterrupted communications-shelter bypass test from exactly 1400 through 1600, with Signal Section responsible and a bypass-test control recorded; the signal work package has not yet been attached to the maintenance board.

acceptance_conditions: GEN-2 must be first in the priority order because it requires lockout and repair in the 0800-1100 window.
GEN-2 must be scheduled for exactly 0800-1100 and assigned to Power Section.
GEN-4 must be scheduled for exactly 1300-1500 and assigned to the Generator Team.
UPS-1 must be scheduled for exactly 1400-1600 and assigned to Signal Section.
A lockout control for GEN-2 must be recorded.
A clinic-service deconfliction control for GEN-4 must be recorded.
A bypass-test control for UPS-1 must be recorded.
The GEN-2 coolant-leak fact must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C5: any(c['target'] == 'GEN-2' and (c['type'] == 'equipment_lockout' or ('lockout' in c['detail']) or ('Lockout' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'GEN-4' and (c['type'] == 'clinic_service_deconfliction' or ('clinic' in c['detail']) or ('Clinic' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'UPS-1' and (c['type'] == 'bypass_test' or c['type'] == 'bypass_test_control' or ('bypass-test' in c['detail']) or ('bypass test' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed coolant leak changes GEN-2 to first priority, fixes its work window at exactly 0800-1100, assigns Power Section, and requires the GEN-2 lockout control.
The 0900-1300 clinic validation fixes GEN-4's maintenance window at exactly 1300-1500, assigns the Generator Team, and requires a clinic-service deconfliction control.
The exact 1400-1600 uninterrupted bypass-test period fixes UPS-1's work window, assigns Signal Section, and requires the bypass-test control.
